byte_limit_scopes.max_request_bytes: Complete action/params request object, not params alone.
byte_limit_scopes.max_result_bytes: Complete result data object, excluding the transport envelope.

lexical_types.runtime: ^[a-z0-9-]{1,64}$; existing media RPC runtime alphabet, independent of optional diagnostics
lexical_types.opaque_id: ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$; exact case; generated opaque nonce, never a URL/path/provider ID

status_rules.malformed_request: Existing controller request rejection before player dispatch

invariants: Every illustrated wire object has exact keys; unknown keys, duplicate JSON keys, null/mistyped booleans, non-finite/fractional integers and oversized UTF-8 payloads are invalid.
All successful results have scope=current_playback. No default-language, profile, per-title/show track memory, Plex part selection, or other durable selection write is permitted.

List is passive and complete, without download, source resolution, playback start, selection, or provider HTTP requests. Unknown catalog returns catalog_incomplete; an actually known empty catalog returns tracks=[].
Track IDs are unique across both kinds within a catalog and never reused for a different row. The same metadata item may have a new ID after catalog invalidation.

Target mode=track requires exactly kind/mode/id, kind is audio|subtitle, and id must name a selectable row of that kind. Mode=off requires exactly kind=subtitle and mode=off; it has no id and requires subtitle_off_supported=true.

Playback token identifies the current logical play item, not its title or provider ID. Source generation identifies the current concrete pipeline/source binding; catalog identifies the complete immutable ID-to-track mapping and its selectable/off support policy.

Runtime, playback, source_generation and catalog are checked at admission and immediately before the initial effect. Changes to source binding or track mapping invalidate old receipts even if the visible item/title is unchanged. An operation's own fenced rebuild continuation follows the separate authority-transfer rule below.

A successful list renews the unchanged catalog receipt for 60000ms. A selection or rejection does not renew it. If context changes, list mints fresh IDs/catalog; old selections are rejected without fallback/remapping.

A native-owned selection-intent epoch is shared by manual and remote audio/subtitle choices. Every newly accepted intent, including an explicit no-op, advances it. At most one selection is pending across both kinds. A newer accepted intent supersedes and cancels all effects/continuations of the old intent even if runtime, source and catalog are unchanged. Invalid/rejected requests do not supersede valid work.

At admission capture an immutable monotonic authority deadline=min(request_expiry, catalog_lease_expiry_at_admission), the logical playback, selection-intent epoch and resolved native target. Expiry uses the original transport deadline, not ACK time. Later list renewal, ACK, queueing or rebuilding cannot extend it. Every effect and continuation checks deadline and intent; expired/superseded work has no further effects.

An operation may transfer authority to the concrete source generation produced by its own explicit rebuild handoff only while runtime, logical playback, captured selection-intent epoch, local policy and immutable deadline still match. The old source generation/catalog retire immediately. The continuation uses the already resolved native target and existing fenced handoff ownership; it never re-resolves the old track ID against a new catalog and never adopts an unrelated new source. Without proven handoff ownership it cancels.

observed state=track requires a same-kind listed track_id and integer age_ms. state=off is subtitle-only with null track_id and integer age_ms. state=not_observed requires null track_id and null age_ms.

Observation comes from current-source backend evidence, never a requested index, selected flag from provider metadata, route plan, queued action, generic playback progress or first video frame. Age is monotonic time since that evidence; invalidating its source clears it.

Select outcome=requested requires observed=null and means admission only. outcome=confirmed requires matching current-context backend evidence generated after admission and under the still-current selection-intent epoch, or a fresh post-admission authoritative read proving the requested target was already selected. Previously cached same-source observations and delayed old events cannot confirm. A subtitle-off confirmation requires positively known backend disabled state, not absent cues. It confirms backend selection, never physical audio audibility or subtitle pixels.

Accepted asynchronous selection may subsequently be superseded, fail or be cancelled. No implicit mutation replay occurs. Ordinary receipt id/status remain available. Follow-up list reports current facts, not proof that a particular past request caused them.

If a selection rebuilds/rebinds the source before confirmation, its result remains requested; old-context confirmation is prohibited. A fresh list may show the new context; v1 adds no correlated asynchronous job/status protocol.

Unsafe labels are replaced by Track N; no URL, filesystem path, token, raw provider identifier, internal stream object or error exception leaves the player. CLI applies its usual safe display projection again.

Capability remains absent until producer/controller/CLI fixtures and genuine native E2E cover list, both selections, subtitle off, stale receipts, no persistence and truthful evidence. Other clients keep old behavior.
